**Engineer's response**

**(1) Second pols and divergence.** Yes, my logs record a second pols. ENG-011 (dag 10, 02:40) reads "geactiveerd: eigen pols voor het datanet, los van de Kroonklok," and ENG-103 describes the design as an own pols in the datatoren cellar. ENG-106 gives the activation as 02:40 and the first measurement as 03:00. The first datanet-side anomaly in my logs is ENG-107 (dag 10, 04:50), a complaint of "half aangekomen" messages. My source does not record when the Burchtader itself diverged, so I cannot date that.

**(2) Numerical readings.** ENG-012 records +38% throughput at dag 10, 03:00. ENG-120 says the figure was still 38% higher on dag 16. For the dag 22 event, ENG-026 and ENG-110 record 3 minuten pakketverlies on poort oost at 04:15, with no percentage. For the dag 24 step-up, ENG-029 and ENG-062 record a 5% increase at 11:00 and 11:05, with tempo unchanged. My source has no latency or sync-offset figures. ENG-061 (dag 12, 10:30) records a 0,1% fine-tuning test, restored to the original setting.

**(3) Constraints and authorization.** My source contains no shutdown constraint, storage limit tied to the polsen, or backup prerequisite for activation. ENG-105 (dag 9) says "Goedkeuring verkregen van hogerhand," without naming the authority. I found no back-up record between dag 9 and the 02:40 activation. Storage pressure is recorded separately: ENG-112 (dag 31) and ENG-045 (dag 33) on schijf 4, and ENG-092 (dag 33) on compressed logs.

**Timestamp mismatch.** My entries show no mismatch. ENG-107 and ENG-026 each have a single time, and ENG-026 matches ENG-110 at 04:15. The Historian's HIS-036 is not in my source, so I cannot confirm or refute the mismatch.

**Correction to my earlier view.** ENG-110 attributes the dag 22 loss to outside hackers. That is my speculation, not evidence. My source records only the loss (ENG-026) and the firewall change (ENG-027). I withdraw the hacker attribution as unsupported.
